proposals: The Department of Fertilizers should publish an official state-wise table of urea sales per hectare of gross cropped area every year, using the Directorate of Economics and Statistics' cropped-area figures, so that the ratio this post had to derive from two departments' releases, read off a chart, becomes a published number anyone can track.

The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare should commission and publish an updated crop-wise, state-wise survey of nitrogen application, replacing the FAO study built on 2003–04 data, so that the claim that a state over-applies urea rests on measured crop-level use rather than on cropping pattern and a national 70 per cent estimate.

The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and ICAR should issue a single reconciled instruction on Fermented Organic Manure — one application window (the gazette label's 15–20 days or ICAR's 7–10 days before sowing) and one pH range (6.0–8.4 or 6.5–7.5) — so that the label and the package of practices stop contradicting each other.

The Department of Fertilizers should publish Market Development Assistance claims received, approved, paid and pending, in tonnes and rupees, alongside FOM, LFOM and PROM sales, so that the gap between ₹111.72 crore released and 20.65 lakh tonnes sold can be read as either a disbursement backlog or volume that never claimed the assistance.

CFQC&TI should publish first-stage state laboratory results for FOM and LFOM by parameter and by state, not only third-stage referrals, so that an actual market failure rate for the new Schedule VIII category is available instead of the filtered 80 per cent figure that reflects only disputed samples.
